audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Moses' birth/rescue, women's agency, Egyptian violence, Midian, covenant remembrance, Divine hearing.

verses.restored: A man from house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi.

familiar.text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

modern.text: Now a man of the house of Levi married a daughter of Levi,

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִ֖ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת בַּת לֵוִֽי

verses.restored: The woman conceived and bore a son; she saw that he was good, and she hid him three months.

familiar.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

modern.text: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.

original.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים

verses.restored: When she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark/basket of papyrus, smeared it with bitumen and pitch, placed the child in it, and set it among reeds by bank of Nile.

familiar.text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

modern.text: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.

original.text: וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר

verses.restored: His sister stood at a distance to know what would be done to him.

familiar.text: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

modern.text: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

original.text: וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ

verses.restored: The daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the Nile, and her young women walked beside the Nile. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her female servant, and she took it.

familiar.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

modern.text: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.

original.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ

verses.restored: She opened and saw him, the child, and look, a boy weeping; she had compassion on him and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.

familiar.text: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

modern.text: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”

original.text: וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה

verses.restored: His sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrew women, so she may nurse the child for you?

familiar.text: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?

modern.text: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד

verses.restored: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Go. The young woman went and called the child's mother.

familiar.text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.

modern.text: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.

original.text: וַתֹּֽאמֶר לָ֥הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֑כִי וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ הָֽעַלְמָ֔ה וַתִּקְרָ֖א אֶת אֵ֥ם הַיָּֽלֶד

verses.restored: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Take this child and nurse him for me, and I myself will give your wages. The woman took the child and nursed him.

familiar.text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

modern.text: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.

original.text: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She called his name Moses, saying, Because from the waters I drew him out.

familiar.text: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

modern.text: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” The Rejection and Flight of Moses (Acts 7:23–29)

original.text: וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ

verses.restored: In those days, when Moses had grown, he went out to his brothers and saw their burdens; he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his brothers.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.

modern.text: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and observed their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו

verses.restored: He turned here and there, and saw no man, and struck the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

familiar.text: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

modern.text: After looking this way and that and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.

original.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל

verses.restored: He went out the second day, and look, two Hebrew men were fighting. He said to the guilty one, Why do you strike your companion?

familiar.text: And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?

modern.text: The next day Moses went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you attacking your companion?”

original.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנֵֽי אֲנָשִׁ֥ים עִבְרִ֖ים נִצִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע לָ֥מָּה תַכֶּ֖ה רֵעֶֽךָ

verses.restored: He said, Who set you as man, prince, and judge over us? Are you saying to kill me as you killed the Egyptian? Moses feared and said, Surely the matter is known.

familiar.text: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.

modern.text: But the man replied, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian? ” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “This thing I have done has surely become known.”

original.text: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר

verses.restored: Pharaoh heard this matter and sought to kill Moses. Moses fled from face of Pharaoh and dwelt in land of Midian; he sat down by a well.

familiar.text: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

modern.text: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר

verses.restored: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water and filled troughs to water their father's flock.

familiar.text: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.

modern.text: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.

original.text: וּלְכֹהֵ֥ן מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֣בַע בָּנ֑וֹת וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה וַתִּדְלֶ֗נָה וַתְּמַלֶּ֨אנָה֙ אֶת הָ֣רְהָטִ֔ים לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת צֹ֥אן אֲבִיהֶֽן

verses.restored: The shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses rose and saved/helped them and watered their flock.

familiar.text: And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

modern.text: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ הָרֹעִ֖ים וַיְגָרְשׁ֑וּם וַיָּ֤קָם מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיּ֣וֹשִׁעָ֔ן וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת צֹאנָֽם

verses.restored: They came to Reuel their father, and he said, Why have you hurried to come today?

familiar.text: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to day?

modern.text: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֕אנָה אֶל רְעוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִיהֶ֑ן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַדּ֛וּעַ מִהַרְתֶּ֥ן בֹּ֖א הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: They said, An Egyptian man rescued us from hand of shepherds, and also drew water for us and watered the flock.

familiar.text: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.

modern.text: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they replied. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”

original.text: וַתֹּאמַ֕רְןָ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י הִצִּילָ֖נוּ מִיַּ֣ד הָרֹעִ֑ים וְגַם דָּלֹ֤ה דָלָה֙ לָ֔נוּ וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת הַצֹּֽאן

verses.restored: He said to his daughters, Where is he? Why did you leave the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.

familiar.text: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.

modern.text: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל בְּנֹתָ֖יו וְאַיּ֑וֹ לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ן אֶת הָאִ֔ישׁ קִרְאֶ֥ן ל֖וֹ וְיֹ֥אכַל לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: Moses was willing to dwell with the man, and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses.

familiar.text: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

modern.text: Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.

original.text: וַיּ֥וֹאֶל מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אֶת הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיִּתֵּ֛ן אֶת צִפֹּרָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ לְמֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: She bore a son, and he called his name Gershom, for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.

familiar.text: And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.

modern.text: And she gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land.” God Hears the Cry of the Israelites

original.text: וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ גֵּרְשֹׁ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר גֵּ֣ר הָיִ֔יתִי בְּאֶ֖רֶץ נָכְרִיָּֽה

verses.restored: In those many days, king of Egypt died. The children of Israel groaned from the service, and they cried out; their cry for help went up to the Divine from the service.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.

modern.text: After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ בַיָּמִ֨ים הָֽרַבִּ֜ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיָּ֨מָת֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיֵּאָנְח֧וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִן הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ וַתַּ֧עַל שַׁוְעָתָ֛ם אֶל הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מִן הָעֲבֹדָֽה

verses.restored: The Divine heard their groaning, and the Divine remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

familiar.text: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

modern.text: So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת נַאֲקָתָ֑ם וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת בְּרִית֔וֹ אֶת אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת יִצְחָ֥ק וְאֶֽת יַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: The Divine saw the children of Israel, and the Divine knew.

familiar.text: And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.

modern.text: God saw the Israelites and took notice.

original.text: וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֖דַע אֱלֹהִֽים

translation_notes: Moses' basket uses tevah/ark language, echoing Noah: life preserved through waters.
Women's agency drives the rescue: mother, sister, Pharaoh's daughter, female servant, and later Midianite daughters.
Moses' first act of resistance is morally complicated and should not be romanticized as clean liberation violence.
Divine hearing/remembering/seeing/knowing forms the turning point.
safety_note: The chapter shows both courageous rescue and dangerous impulsive violence. It should not be used to sanctify vigilantism. The deeper liberation movement begins with Divine hearing and covenant remembrance.
